findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue. The palette gives that blue to links and the button. On an article page, a large run of blue text that does nothing reads like a link. It also weakens the blue as the one colour that means you can act on something.
findings.who_objects: A reader at a development bank, reading one of Mark's articles, would tap the quote expecting a link. The founder would also object, because the tile sets this as the pattern for every post Angélique adds, and the house rule says a colour that marks links or actions never colours text that isn't a link.

findings.where: First screen: the headline and the line under it (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The headline is a name and job title, and the line under it is in the third person ("from a former Lead Lawyer…"). Nowhere on the first screen does Mark speak in his own words. The brief carries over "a serif headline in Mark's own words" and asks for one strong personal line, so this reads like a firm's directory entry, not the advisor himself.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brand sheet (§5) asks for a personal, approachable voice where the individual is the brand. Visitors would get a CV label instead of the person they are deciding whether to contact.

findings.where: First screen: "Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience" in the line under the headline
findings.fault: The proof next to the main action is a size claim, not something a reader can check. The same line also says nothing of who the advice is for (development agencies and banks) or which regions it covers.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank procurement staff judge an advisor by the kind of project, the region and named roles, not by years. The client values also ask for confidence without boasts.

findings.where: First screen: the "Get in touch" button (a mailto link); the page has no footer
findings.fault: The only real way to get in touch is a mailto button that hides the address. Nowhere on the page is the email shown in full as text a visitor can copy, so someone without a desktop mail client gets nothing when they click.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency staffer on a locked-down work machine, or on webmail, clicks and nothing useful opens. They then have to search for Mark's address before they can write to him.

findings.where: Nav bar: "Articles" and "Blog" side by side (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: Two nav items name what looks like the same thing. The article specimen itself is headed "MMM Infra Blog No. 8", so a visitor can't tell which item holds Mark's writing on PPP law.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for Mark's published thinking has to guess between two items, or open both.

findings.fault: At phone width the lockup drops "Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services" and shows only the mark and "MMM INFRA". That is a version of the logo the client does not hold, and on a phone nothing on the first screen spells out what MMM stands for.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder: the brand sheet (§4) defines the logo as the mark with the descriptor to its right, and a new version needs the client's yes. A phone visitor also loses the line that says what the firm is.

findings.where: Motion sketch and first screen as a whole
findings.fault: The tile does not answer two client values every direction must answer. There is no quiet moment before the words and the button appear (value 2): the heading rises at 0 ms with the button already in view. And nothing shows how the logo is built in grey and blue (value 7), although the direction card calls the mark "the only picture".
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for calm first and for the logo to be built by the opening animation. The animation round (#9) would also have no motion principle from this look to draw on.

findings.where: Style tile: section labels. "Texture" and "Motion sketch" have a hairline under them; "Palette", "Type pair" and "An article page" do not (desktop-02, phone-01, phone-02)
findings.fault: Labels of the same kind are treated two ways, so some sections look ruled off and others don't, for no reason a reader can see.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the layout round, who take this tile as the system to build from, and would not know which label style is the rule.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the principle words "precise, light, quick" (desktop-02, phone-02)
findings.fault: A display-sized heading is set in Source Sans semibold, though the tile's own type pair says the sans is for "the nav, buttons, labels and dates only" and Gelasio is for headings.
findings.who_objects: The founder or a later designer reading the tile as the type rules, who finds the tile breaking its own rule.

findings.where: Type pair: the "Source Sans 3" specimen, alone in the right column (desktop-02)
findings.fault: The Source Sans specimen sits in the right column straight under the Texture section, with the "Type pair" label far to the left. Its nearness to Texture and the open gap beside Gelasio make it read as part of Texture, not as the second half of the pair.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reading the tile quickly, may not see that the two faces are a pair.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the "Play again" control (desktop-03, phone-03)
findings.fault: A button that replays the animation on this page is styled as an underlined link. A link look means it takes you somewhere, not that it does something here.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, previewing the tile, may expect it to open a new page. The pattern would also teach the layout round to style actions as links.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the easing-curve plot (desktop-03, phone-02/03)
findings.fault: The curve sits in a bare box with no labels saying what each axis is (time and progress), and its ends run past the frame. It is hard to read as a plot of the easing.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who is not a motion designer and is asked to judge the motion principle from this picture.
